content:
rachel_sales: Heads up - GammaBank POC is stuck. They resolve our private hostname to an IP but TLS validation fails for their app and they see 403 in logs. Demo in 20h. Can we triage?
eli_engineer: Do we have the exact IP they resolve and the curl/openssl output? 403+TLS usually indicates they hit the wrong backend (eg internal ELB) or proxy/OCSP issues.
marta_netops: They reported DNS -> 192.168.250.77. That's not one of our VPCE interface IPs. Could be split-horizon / private hosted zone pointing to an internal LB. Ask them for `dig +short api.redwood.internal @<resolver>` and `dig +short api.redwood.internal` from a pod.
rachel_sales: They pasted this from their app node: `curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/health --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:192.168.250.77` response shows TLS cert CN=internal-nginx.local and then `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden {"error":"AccessDenied","message":"principal not authorized"}`
kevin_sre: That CN is a red flag. It means the TLS handshake terminated at their local gateway/loadbalancer, not our endpoint. Also ask them to run `openssl s_client -connect 192.168.250.77:443 -servername api.redwood.internal -status` to check OCSP stapling and the cert chain. If OCSP requests are blocked by firewall it can cause clients to fail pinning/validation.
juno_security: Also request the JWT claims (sanitized) or at least `iss` and `org_id`. But given the cert mismatch, auth won't even get to our ingress.
diag-bot: running vpce:check-routes for vpce-0d1e2f3a - queued
eli_engineer: Hypotheses: 1) Their Route53 private hosted zone contains an A record for api.redwood.internal pointing at an internal LB. 2) Their corporate DNS forwarder resolves to a cached on-prem record. 3) A sidecar/proxy in the pod rewrites hosts.
marta_netops: Commands for them to run and paste: `dig +short api.redwood.internal @169.254.169.253` (instance resolver), `dig +short api.redwood.internal @<their-corp-dns>`, and `grep api.redwood.internal /etc/hosts` in the app container. Also `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-endpoint-id,Values=vpce-* --query 'VpcEndpoints[*].DnsEntries'` from their ops if they can.
rachel_sales: They ran `openssl s_client -connect 192.168.250.77:443 -servername api.redwood.internal -status` and pasted the top lines: `OCSP response: no response sent`, `Server certificate: subject CN=internal-nginx.local, issuer CN=Corp Internal CA`.
\e_li_engineer: That confirms TLS is terminating on their side (corp LB/proxy) and OCSP stapling isn't from our side. For the demo we can either: 1) have ops update DNS so api.redwood.internal resolves to the VPCE IP (quick fix), 2) request their proxy team to allow TLS passthrough to the endpoint IP so our cert is presented, or 3) temporarily use a public staging domain that bypasses their private DNS.
\e_li_engineer: Also check if their egress firewall is blocking outbound OCSP queries to the CA; if the client requires OCSP and proxy strips stapled responses, validation can fail.
juno_security: If customers insist on MITM proxy for inspection, we'll need to document our recommended proxy config: allow passthrough for the VPCE range, or install a corporate CA into the client truststore and agree to cert re-signing (not ideal). For long POCs we can support mutual TLS as an option but that requires cert exchange and provisioning which takes time.
kevin_sre: For immediate steps: 1) replace the private hosted zone record or remove conflicting ALIAS/A record so DNS points to our VPCE IP; 2) if they can't change DNS, test from a bastion in the same VPC with `curl --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:<vpce-ip> https://api.redwood.internal/health` to prove our side works; 3) provide a short-lived public endpoint if they need to demo without changing their DNS.
diag-bot: vpce route check completed - no route anomalies detected on our side for vpce-0d1e2f3a
marta_netops: I'll draft an email with the exact dig/openssl commands and a minimal DNS troubleshooting checklist for their infra team. Also include a snippet to check Route53 private hosted zones: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-xxxx`
rachel_sales: They're also asking about POC pricing if we need to set up an isolated tunnel or dedicate a temporary public endpoint for their security team. What's our short-term POC offering?
\eli_engineer: Sales can offer a 14-day isolated POC with a temporary dedicated tunnel (VPN) or a short-lived public staging hostname. Pricing is handled by sales ops but technically feasible within 24-48h for a small throughput cap. Note: mutual TLS onboarding would push timeline ~1-2 weeks.
juno_security: I'll prepare a brief note on security tradeoffs for each option for their reviewers (passthrough vs MITM vs mutual TLS).
kevin_sre: Closing: get them to run the dig/openssl checks and either fix the private hosted zone or allow passthrough. If they need us to provision a staged public hostname for the demo, we can, but sales ops will need to approve pricing.
rachel_sales: Thanks team - I'll push the checklist to GammaBank and request the outputs. Will update this thread when they reply.
